svg.title: Four mathematical tasks for composing partial views
svg.desc: Four operations with distinct mathematical precedents and limits. Logical dependencies are shown through the shared qualification conditions, not as a mandatory serial execution protocol.
svg.text: Four mathematical tasks for composing partial views
Each operation needs both a representation and a limit on inference.
The numbering follows the argument; it does not prescribe a serial implementation.
01 · INTERPRET ROLES
Recognize A/B/C/D
Qualified assertions relative to a declared process and
frame can represent the four functional roles.
Limit: producer meaning, capability and evidence are
needed. Open C/D cannot be exhaustively classified.
02 · RELATE SCOPES
Justify the correspondence
Typed contexts and partial maps can represent where
declarations admit a common question.
Limit: a common label or MSCA is not enough.
Cockett–Lack represents partiality; semantic validity
needs separate grounds. [§3.2]
03 · COMPOSE SUMMARIES
Preserve a useful distinction
Task-relative abstraction can support exact answers or
sound conservative answer sets. Attributed
aggregation can retain distinct declarations.
Limit: convergence is not truth or source
independence. Streaming-space bounds are not
communication bounds. Total cost remains open. [§4]
04 · REQUALIFY
Give a property-specific direction
Versioned judgments, partial orders and signed
comparisons of warranted bounds can express
contextual change.
Limit: requalification needs grounds. Increased
assessability need not mean lower risk; a direction is
not a universal A/B/C/D score. [§6]
The conditions must survive composition
The receiving review still needs compatible scope, interpretation, provenance and current grounds. Success in
one operation cannot compensate for a missing correspondence or qualification in another.
The bounded opportunity
Compatible metadata may expose a changed basis for collective reliance that operative outputs conceal. Useful
requalification also requires those distinctions to survive composition and arrive in time.

a.text: Selective overview · 00M v0.8, §§3–7; 00N v0.7, §§1.3, 3.2 · Plausibility is not engineering feasibility.
